extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent office officials, and litigants in the United Kingdom (practitioners of 1883-era patent law)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards under the Patents and Designs Act 1883 governing injunctions, inspection, accounts, certificates, exhibitions, assignments, models, foreign-vessel use, existing patents, and registration of designs. A practitioner's guide to what the Court, Comptroller, and Board of Trade may require or permit in patent/design proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory injunction application timing and form
rubrics_metrics.description: By R. S. C. Order LI. Rule 6, an application for an interlocutory injunction under sect. 25, sub-sect. 8 of the Judicature Act, 1873, may be made by the plaintiff by motion, either ex parte or with notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally the injunction will not be granted on an ex parte application except in case of emergency. A notice of motion must be a two clear days' notice, unless special leave be given to the contrary (R. S. C. Order LII. r. 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits supporting injunction applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits in support of the application must clearly and accurately set forth the legal title of the plaintiff; that he believed at the time of making the application (not at the time the patent was obtained) that the patentee was the first and true inventor; and that the invention had not been practised at the time the patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nature of the alleged infringements must also be particularly stated (cases cited: Gardiner v. Broadbent; Whitton v. Jennings; Hull v. Thompson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's discretion and conditional terms for injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court has discretionary power to grant or withhold an injunction and may do so on such terms and conditions as appear just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An injunction may be granted on an undertaking by the plaintiff to be liable for any damages the defendant may incur (Plimpton v. Spiller); or may be refused upon an undertaking by the defendant to keep an account of profits (Bridson v. McAlpine); or ordered to stand over until trial. A perpetual injunction may sometimes be granted by consent on interlocutory application but is usually obtained at final trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and urgent notice methods for orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of order must be before 6 p.m., or on Saturdays before 2 p.m. (R. S. C. LXIV. r. 11), and it is sufficient if an office copy be exhibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice may be given by telegram in cases of urgency (Ex parte Langley, Re Bishop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement and adequacy of seeking interlocutory injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where obtaining an injunction is a substantial object of the action the writ should be endorsed accordingly (Goulsbourne v. Golsbourne).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to apply for an interlocutory injunction will not preclude asking for a perpetual one at hearing, but if no such prior application was made the patentee will be required to establish a clear and unexceptional title (Bacon v. Jones; Patent Type Founding Co. v. Walter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction against threatened infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction may be obtained against the threatened infringement of a patent (Frearson v. Lowe), but the application would require to be made under sect. 25, sub-s. 8 of the Judicature Act, 1873, unless made in 'an action for infringement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the threat is a substantial part of the relief sought, follow the interlocutory procedure in sect. 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages in lieu of or in addition to injunctions (Lord Cairns' Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Lord Cairns' Act (21 & 22 Vict. c. 27, s. 2), the Court may give damages in addition to or in substitution for an injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether monetary relief rather than injunctive relief better serves justice in the circumstances; the statute authorises substitution or addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of defendant's works—necessity and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspection of the defendant's works and machinery will only be ordered where the Court is satisfied that the inspection is essential to the plaintiff's case (Bailey v. Kynock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection may be limited (e.g., restricted to one machine of each class sold—The Singer Sewing Machine Co. v. Wilson), may exclude inspection by the plaintiff (Flower v. Llaydy), and will be refused if important trade secrets would be disclosed or if alleged infringement took place abroad (Piggott v. The Anglo-American Telegraph Company; Neilson v. Belts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for applications for inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: An application under Order L. Rule 3 cannot be made to a Master in the Queen's Bench Division (Order LIV. r. 12(e)); it may be made to a Judge in Chambers by summons, or to a Judge in Court by motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of the application must be given (Ord. LI. Rule 6), and two clear days must elapse between service of notice of motion and the day named for hearing unless leave be given to the contrary (Order LII. Rule 5). Forms referenced: App. A., Daniel's Chancery Forms, Seton on Decrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim account as alternative to interlocutory injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: On an application for an interlocutory injunction the Court may instead of granting such injunction order an account to be kept of all future sales and profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An account of past profits is not generally ordered until final judgment (Vidi v. Smith). The Court has extensive power to order accounts at any stage (Order XXXIII. Rule 2). Forms: App. A., Seton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election between account of profits and damages
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee is not at final judgment entitled to both an account of profits and an inquiry as to damages against the same person, but must elect which he will take (Beckett? Vitre v. Belts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the patentee may obtain an account against manufacturing persons and damages against persons using the infringing articles (Funn v. Bibby).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent expiration and plaintiff delay on accounting relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The expiration of the patent before the action comes on for hearing will not deprive the plaintiff of his right to an account (Fox v. Dellestable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But regard will be had to the circumstances and an account may be refused where the plaintiff delayed taking proceedings for years after the patent expired (Smith v. London & South Western Railway Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on entitlement to accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: One of two joint owners is not entitled to an account as against another joint owner (Mathers v. Green); and a patentee cannot obtain an account against a manufacturer who is an agent to take fixed sums and pay a royalty (Moxon v. Bright).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also authority regarding accounts between assignee and licensee (Bergmann v. Macmillan) and in bankruptcy (Watson v. Holliday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of books and staying account proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In aid of an account the defendant may be ordered to produce his books for inspection (Saxby v. Easterbrook). Proceedings under an account may be stayed pending an appeal (Muir v. Young).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of order references: App. A., Seton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate that patent validity was questioned (costs consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement the Court or a judge may certify that the validity of the patent came in question; if so certified then in any subsequent action for infringement the successful plaintiff shall have full costs as between solicitor and client unless the Court or judge trying the action certifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate may be given by 'the Court or a judge' (not necessarily the trial judge), need not be 'on the record' nor required to be given in evidence in the subsequent action. The certificate applies only to subsequent suits, not to costs of the first trial (Pann v. Bibby; Davenport v. Eylands).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for groundless threats of proceedings by patentee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person claiming to be patentee threatens another with legal proceedings by circulars, advertisements, or otherwise in respect of alleged manufacture, use, sale, or purchase, any person aggrieved thereby may bring an action and may obtain an injunction against continuance of such threats and recover damages if the alleged acts were not in fact infringements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This remedy exists without the necessity of showing reasonable and probable cause where damages are sought; but the section does not apply if the person making threats with due diligence commences and prosecutes an action for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior case law on threats (Hahey v. Brotherhood)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under prior case law a patentee who threatened purchasers was not liable to damages unless he acted mala fide (without reasonable and probable cause), though an injunction might be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory provision in this Act alters that position by providing for damages without requiring proof of reasonable and probable cause in specified circumstances; injunction still available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent must be for one invention only (claims allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent may be in the form in the First Schedule and shall be granted for one invention only, but may contain more than one claim; it shall not be competent in an action or other proceeding to object to a patent on the ground that it comprises more than one invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be hard to decide what constitutes 'one invention' vs more; the examiner is not required to report specially on this point but may report that the specification has not been prepared in the 'prescribed manner' if necessary. A claim is not necessary in a provisional specification (sect. 5(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of patent to personal representative (timing and declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person possessed of an invention dies without making application for a patent, application may be made by, and a patent granted to, his legal representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such application must be made within six months of the death and must contain a declaration by the legal representative that he believes such person to be the true and first inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of true and first inventor against fraudulent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted to the true and first inventor shall not be invalidated by an application in fraud of him, or by provisional protection obtained thereon, or by any use or publication of the invention subsequent to that fraudulent application during the period of fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section aims to protect the true and first inventor after he has obtained a patent from consequences of fraudulent applications by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of patent rights for particular places
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may assign his patent for any place in or part of the United Kingdom, or Isle of Man, as effectually as if the patent were originally granted to extend to that place or part only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends prior law which only allowed assignment of rights for England, Scotland, or Ireland; further precedents and forms are in Appendix E and Patents Forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate patent where lost or destroyed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is lost or destroyed, or its non-production is accounted for to the satisfaction of the comptroller, the comptroller may at any time cause a duplicate thereof to be sealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must state his interest; see Patents Forms (Form N) and fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers and remit of law officers in patent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Law officers may examine witnesses on oath and administer oaths for that purpose, and from time to time make, alter, and rescind rules regulating references and appeals to the law officer and the practice and procedure thereunder; law officers may order costs to be paid and such orders may be made a rule of Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings before law officers include appeals from comptroller decisions (refusing to accept an application or requiring amendment), disputes about same inventions in multiple applications, refusal to accept complete specification, opposition to grant, and amendments of specification. See Patents Rules for detailed procedures and enforcement (R. S. C. O. XLIT. r. 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition of invention without prejudice to patent rights (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibition of an invention at an industrial or international exhibition certified by the Board of Trade, or publication of a description of the invention during the period of the exhibition, or use of the invention for the purpose of the exhibition in the place where held, shall not prejudice the right to apply for and obtain provisional protection and a patent, provided conditions are complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (a) exhibitor must, before exhibiting, give the comptroller the prescribed notice (Form O) of intention to do so; (b) application for a patent must be made before or within six months from the date of the opening of the exhibition. The notice requires a 10s stamp and a brief description/drawings if necessary (Patents Rules, 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of patent journal, indexes and requirements for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller shall issue periodically an illustrated journal of patented inventions, and make provision for keeping on sale copies of such journal and of all complete specifications of patents in force with accompanying drawings; and continue indexes and abridgments as he deems fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By Patents Rule 31 every applicant must, in addition to drawings in the complete specification, furnish the comptroller with a drawing illustrative of the feature(s) of novelty not exceeding sixteen square inches, accompanied by a concise explanatory statement on foolscap paper and legibly written or printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Museum management and models on payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Control and management of the existing Patent Museum are vested in the Department of Science and Art; the Department may at any time require a patentee to furnish a model of his invention on payment to the patentee of the cost of manufacture of the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount payable in case of dispute to be settled by the Board of Trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patented invention in foreign vessels within UK jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not prevent the use of an invention for the purposes of navigation of a foreign vessel within the jurisdiction of Her Majesty's Courts in the United Kingdom or Isle of Man, provided it is not used therein for or in connection with the manufacture or preparation of anything intended to be sold in or exported from the United Kingdom or Isle of Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not extend to vessels of foreign states whose laws empower their subjects to prevent use in British vessels in their ports/waters under reciprocal conditions. The Secretary of State may waive the benefit of this section in respect of any particular invention; communications concerning munitions of war to the Secretary do not amount to publication (sect. 43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Act to existing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of this Act relating to applications for patents and proceedings thereon shall have effect only in respect of applications made after commencement of the Act; every patent granted before commencement or on an application then pending shall remain unaffected by provisions relating to compulsory licences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all other respects (including amount and time of payment of fees) the Act shall extend to patents granted before commencement. Instruments required to be left or filed in the Great Seal Patent Office shall be deemed to be so left or filed if left or filed before or after commencement in the Patent Office. Notices and Rules (e.g., Patents Rules) govern transitional arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of designs—eligibility and application content
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may, on application by any person claiming to be proprietor of any new or original design not previously published in the United Kingdom, register the design under this Part of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be made in the prescribed form (First Schedule or other prescribed form), left or sent to the Patent Office in the prescribed manner, and must contain a statement of the nature of the design and the class or classes of goods in which the applicant desires registration. The same design may be registered in more than one class. In case of doubt as to class, the comptroller may decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of design registration and appeal to Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may, if he thinks fit, refuse to register any design presented for registration, but any person aggrieved by such refusal may appeal to the Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board of Trade shall, if required, hear the applicant and the comptroller, and may make an order determining whether, and subject to what conditions, registration is to be permitted.
